items.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
items.snippet: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

items.title: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts
items.snippet: A massive study involving more than 415,000 Americans has uncovered a concerning connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts. Researchers found that adults with the disorder had 57% higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts, with women and younger adults facing particularly elevated risks.

items.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
items.snippet: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

items.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide
items.snippet: A massive study of more than 340,000 adults found that moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death, while even light consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was linked to increased risk. Although heavy drinking was harmful regardless of beverage type, the findings suggest that the relationship between alcohol and health may be more complicated than previously thought.
